A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of CanFields with matching core equations, experiments and figures. v2 ends after its references; v3 additionally includes supplementary material. That material can be compared as newly included documentation, without assuming all its experiments were newly performed.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and interpolation experiments on DeformingThings4D, CAPE and DFAUST, alongside component ablations and runtime measurements in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and includes additional baseline controls, quantitative missing-region results in Table A1, and supplementary robustness, application and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The consolidator, SIREN canonical shape, Fourier/MLP velocity mixture, losses in Equations 1–10 and mesh-flow inference are retained. Supplementary architecture details and the SALD substitution for the already-mentioned missing-normal experiment expand documentation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: The principal datasets remain DeformingThings4D, CAPE, DFAUST and Thingi10K. v3 adds demonstrated textured-scan and texture-animation applications, previously listed only as potential applications, and explicitly evaluates more severe missing-region inputs in Section E.6. Noise, sparsity and missing-normal tests were already mentioned in v2.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets are retained. v3 adds NISE and screened-Poisson reconstruction with ULSM shape matching in Figure A16, and examines SIREN variants of NDF, NVFi and OFlow in Figure 8. NVFi’s described adaptation changes from NDF’s pipeline to adapted OFlow; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects rerunning experiments or correcting their description.

E3.justification: The main 10–25-input-frame, 50-interpolated-frame evaluation and metrics remain unchanged. v3 adds SIREN substitution controls, a three-frame raw-scan comparison, a rerun with missing-region ratios of 0.35–0.63, and a static SIREN reconstruction control. Newly stated benchmark counts and fitting budgets are disclosures, not established changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands the available analyses through the baseline-SIREN study, velocity-weight sensitivity, noise, point/frame sparsity and missing-normal evaluations, and rapid-motion and fine-detail failure studies. v2 contains the main component and regularizer ablations and mentions several supplementary checks, but does not include their detailed evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Temporal means and worst-case scores remain the reporting practice; the consolidator’s learned confidence scores are not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. v3 adds substantial supplementary results, including Table A1: mean IoU on deerFEL_WalkhuntedRM is 89.06% for CanFields versus 80.01% for DSR. Additional findings cover SIREN baseline degradation, robustness, texture propagation and reconstruction failures.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds a Picard–Lindelof-based argument for diffeomorphic, bijective and reversible flow, distinguishing the numerical approximation from the continuous flow. The existing pullback, ODE and loss equations remain unchanged; the supplementary formulations primarily elaborate them rather than introduce a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly foreground arbitrary-length interpolation and diffeomorphic motion, while the second contribution shifts from frequency-bias decoupling to smooth velocity-field design. The central claims of unsupervised joint fitting, temporal coherence and superior reconstruction robustness remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains why SIREN worsens baseline fitting, attributes fine-detail saturation to the canonical representation, and documents dependence on normals. It expands v2’s fixed-topology assumption and briefly listed limitations into concrete applicability boundaries and failure explanations in Sections E.3–E.6.

D1.justification: v3 supplies layer widths and activations, 20 articulation segments, exact loss schedules, solver tolerances, benchmark counts, fitting budgets and application procedures. Access information changes from a promised public release to a project-page link. A limited regression is the omission of the five ablation sequence names explicitly listed in v2.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands its positioning through a Shape Evolution discussion and a separate Dataset Learning category, including NISE, ISD and 4Deform. New citations support curriculum learning, neural smoothness and ODE foundations, while the distinction from fixed-length dataset-trained methods becomes more central.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the related-work, method and evaluation prose are rewritten. Training/testing terminology becomes fitting/interpolation, interpolation evaluation precedes raw-scan robustness, and v3 adds a structured supplement with a questions-and-answers subsection.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1, moves the pipeline from Figure 7 to Figure 3, and relocates motion segmentation from Figure 6 to Figure A2. It adds the SIREN comparison, consolidator architecture diagram, numerous supplementary visualizations and Table A1, alongside extensive placement and caption revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves a substantial documentation gap by supplying architecture, optimization schedules and solver settings that v2 deferred to absent supplementary material. SIREN controls and concrete robustness and failure evidence make the design choices and applicability limits substantially easier to assess. These gains outweigh the unexplained NVFi adaptation change and omitted ablation sequence names; the main performance numbers remain unchanged.
